problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a specialized courier circuit connecting nine regional hubs with the following geographical positions:

Hub Alpha: Coordinates (125,28)  
Hub Beta: Coordinates (15,156)  
Hub Gamma: Coordinates (179,119)  
Hub Delta: Coordinates (157,161)  
Hub Epsilon: Coordinates (86,166)  
Hub Zeta: Coordinates (31,174)  
Hub Eta: Coordinates (182,159)  
Hub Theta: Coordinates (75,32)  
Hub Iota: Coordinates (99,75)

The travel distances between hubs, measured in kilometers, are precisely known:

Alpha to Gamma: 105.8 km  
Alpha to Delta: 136.8 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 143.4 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 173.6 km  
Alpha to Eta: 142.9 km  
Alpha to Theta: 50.2 km  
Alpha to Iota: 53.7 km  
Beta to Gamma: 168.1 km  
Beta to Delta: 142.1 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 71.7 km  
Beta to Zeta: 24.1 km  
Beta to Eta: 167.0 km  
Beta to Theta: 137.8 km  
Beta to Iota: 116.7 km  
Gamma to Delta: 47.4 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 104.2 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 157.9 km  
Gamma to Eta: 40.1 km  
Gamma to Theta: 135.6 km  
Gamma to Iota: 91.3 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 71.2 km  
Delta to Zeta: 126.7 km  
Delta to Eta: 25.1 km  
Delta to Theta: 152.9 km  
Delta to Iota: 103.7 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 55.6 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 96.3 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 134.5 km  
Epsilon to Iota: 91.9 km  
Zeta to Eta: 151.7 km  
Zeta to Theta: 148.7 km  
Zeta to Iota: 120.1 km  
Eta to Theta: 166.1 km  
Eta to Iota: 118.1 km  
Theta to Iota: 49.2 km

Due to a permanent infrastructure limitation, no direct route exists between Hub Alpha and Hub Beta.  
Furthermore, a regulatory condition mandates that exactly one of the following two key connections must be part of the final circuit: the link between Hub Beta and Hub Gamma, or the link between Hub Gamma and Hub Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed tour that visits each hub exactly once and returns to the origin.
